title: Shift assignment boundary review
lede: The month grid is now a coverage and conflict review surface; consequential crew edits move through the Event's private working schedule and release together after review.

stats.n: Measured in the same 11-event Preview data set at 1440×900
Video and Photo before; Video, Photo, Social, and Comms after
Every row still links to its Event; the action is now labelled Manage crew

sections.heading: Assignment review, without live per-cell edits
sections.note: Same Preview database, August 2026, All review filter, top-of-page scroll position, dark system theme, and 1440×900 viewport. The baseline uses the current tree with only the three changed assignment-grid components restored from HEAD.

pairs.title: Month assignment grid
pairs.sub: Look for the working-schedule handoff, visible crew areas, and the removal of inline mutation controls.
pairs.beforeCap: Before: assignment, removal, call-time, and slot controls competed with coverage review inside every cell.
pairs.afterCap: After: the grid scans as coverage state; Manage crew opens the Event-owned private working schedule.

changes.h: Review and mutation shared one surface
changes.was: The 11-event grid rendered 115 live mutation buttons for assignment, removal, call times, and slot add/delete, bypassing the Event working-copy release boundary.
changes.now: Cells are read-only coverage summaries. Individual changes enter through the Event's Manage crew link, while preview-first bulk assignment remains available.

changes.was: Nothing on the page explained why bulk and individual changes had different release behavior.
changes.now: A persistent banner says the grid reviews coverage/conflicts and that Event crew changes release together after review.

changes.h: Cell controls hid the month picture
changes.was: Only two crew-area columns fit in the initial desktop viewport because each cell reserved room for editing controls.
changes.now: All four configured crew-area columns fit at the same viewport and with the same event data.

verification: 73 schedule/shift/trade test files: 520 tests pass, including primary and secondary area eligibility, approval-time state drift, transactional human/system audit actions, notifications, and retired-route handoffs.
Web gates: TypeScript, ESLint, and npm run build:app pass.
Authenticated local render: current and isolated HEAD-baseline assignment grids loaded the same Preview data; DOM measurement confirmed 115 → 0 table buttons and 11 → 11 Event links.
Native gates: iOS project consistency, drift checks, relevant source-contract tests, and the pinned iPhone 16 Pro / iOS 26.5 Xcode build pass.
notes: The source and authenticated web render are verified locally. Deadline-driven escalate-then-approve timing still needs an authenticated deployed workflow run.
No deployment, production mutation, App Store upload, or TestFlight acceptance was performed in this slice.
